# Snowflakings

> Snowflakings is a free, browser-based paper snowflake designer. You draw cuts on a picture of folded paper (a square folded into a 30° wedge with 12 layers) and it instantly shows the unfolded six-point snowflake. It also makes word snowflakes and prints real-size cutting templates (PDF).

Snowflakings runs entirely in the browser. There is no account and no upload, and designs auto-save locally. It is useful for crafters, teachers, kids' activities, holiday decorations and anyone who wants to plan a paper snowflake before cutting.

## What it does
- Draw freehand, straight-line and circle cuts on the folded wedge; every cut repeats 12 times with six-fold mirror symmetry.
- Live unfolded preview, including which pieces fall away (click a piece to keep it instead).
- Sketch layer: plan guide lines first, then trace them into cuts.
- Word cut-out: type up to 7 letters that are symmetric top-to-bottom (B, C, D, E, H, I, K, l, O, t, X). The word repeats around all six arms, from the tip (first letter) toward the centre (last letter). Options: slant the letters to follow the wedge (curved or straight-line), let the first letter form the snowflake's edge, or fill the arm's full width with a thin connecting bar.
- Top trim shapes: flat (hexagon), point, star and round.
- Import SVG cut lines; export PNG; export an SVG template.
- Print / Save as PDF: a real-size cutting template for 6", 8.5", 10", 12", 15 cm or 20 cm paper, with a scale bar to check it printed at 100%.
- Save design / Open design as a .json file.

## How to fold paper for a six-point snowflake
1. Fold a square sheet in half diagonally to make a triangle.
2. Fold the triangle in half; the right-angle corner becomes the snowflake's centre.
3. With the centre pointing down, divide the top into three equal 30° slices.
4. Fold the right slice over the middle, then the left slice over the top.
5. Cut straight across the uneven top (the "top trim").
6. Trace the printed template onto the wedge, cut every red line, and unfold.
